title: Replicating Cross-Model Feature Matching on Multilingual Models: XLM-R vs mBERT

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Multilingual AI systems are deployed in high-stakes contexts globally. If interpretability tools fail on multilingual models due to cross-lingual compression, this is a concrete safety monitoring blind spot. The chain from feature universality to safety monitoring effectiveness is clear.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training SAEs on XLM-R and mBERT activations from scratch requires meaningful compute and SAE training expertise. Working with multilingual corpora and parallel translation data adds data engineering complexity. Beginners would struggle with the full pipeline.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple models, SAE training on each, cross-model feature matching, multilingual data curation, and cross-lingual vs within-language comparisons. This is effectively several experiments combined. Difficult to complete in 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
